correct_completion: I would give students more time.
full_sentence: If I were the teacher, I would give students more time.
acceptable_variants: I would certainly give students more time.
I'd give the students more time to finish.

options.text: I will give students more time.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' describes a real future plan. The hypothetical 'if I were' clause needs 'would' in the main clause.

options.text: I would give students more time.
I would have given students more time.
options.why_wrong: 'Would have given' refers to the past, but the 'if' clause describes a present imaginary situation with 'were'.
The simple present states a fact, but the imaginary situation requires a conditional main clause with 'would'.

explanation: The stem uses 'were' in an imaginary present situation, which is the subjunctive form used with all subjects in this structure. The main clause must use 'would' plus the base verb. Turkish speakers often use the indicative or a simple tense in the main clause, because Turkish marks hypothetical meaning with suffixes rather than with a separate auxiliary verb.
translation: Öğretmen olsaydım, öğrencilere daha fazla zaman verirdim.
